data.title: US judge rejects CFTC emergency bid to block New York from policing Kalshi
data.description:
By Jonathan Stempel

A federal judge rejected on Friday the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's request to temporarily block New York Attorney General Letitia James from pursuing an enforcement case against prediction markets operator Kalshi.

US District Judge Lorna Schofield in Manhattan said the CFTC had "not established a likelihood of success on the merits" of its argument that federal law preempted states from enforcing their own gambling laws against prediction markets operators, including requirements that operators obtain gaming licenses.

The CFTC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Schofield noted that three federal appeals courts have ruled that states could regulate Kalshi, while a fourth said New Jersey could not.

That split increases the likelihood that the US Supreme Court will eventually decide the issue.

Schofield ruled one day after US District Judge Vernon Broderick in Manhattan granted New York's request to move its lawsuit against Kalshi back to the Manhattan state court where it was filed on July 31.

That prompted the CFTC to make what it called an emergency request for a late-afternoon hearing to temporarily halt New York's enforcement activity.

The regulator said moving the case left "no practical barrier to New York moving full steam ahead" against Kalshi.

James alleged that Kalshi should have obtained a New York State Gaming Commission license to operate its platform, where people trade on the predicted outcomes of sports, elections and other events.

She said such platforms can encourage problem gambling and endanger people's financial, emotional and physical health.

The CFTC regards Kalshi's contracts as "swaps" and has sued 12 states to defend what it calls its exclusive jurisdiction over US derivatives markets.

data.title: NVDA Stock Clocks Worst Week In 18 Years As SEC Reportedly Probes Its Accounting Practices
data.description:
Key points:
  • Reuters said it could not immediately establish when the inquiry began or which specific accounting matters are under review. 
  • NVDA stock lost 23% this week, its worst since October 2008. 
  • The reported accounting focus adds to existing challenges for Nvidia as investors remain bothered by revelations involving former CEO Jensen Huang’s personal relationships

Shares of Nvidia (NVDA) tumbled 14% on Friday, extending a steep multi-week slide following a report that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the company.

The agency is scrutinizing Nvidia’s accounting practices, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. The Wall Street Journal had reported earlier in the week that the SEC was investigating the chipmaker but could not determine the probe’s focus.

Reuters said it could not immediately establish when the inquiry began or which specific accounting matters are under review. An investigation does not prove wrongdoing and often end without enforcement action, the report noted.

NVDA stock lost 23% this week, its worst since October 2008. The stock also clocked seven consecutive weeks of losses after Friday’s closing.

Regulatory Scrutiny Builds On Nvidia

The reported accounting focus adds to existing challenges for Nvidia as investors remain bothered by revelations involving former CEO Jensen Huang’s personal relationships, including one with Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy—an allegation Beijing has denied. Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia customer.

Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair last week without naming Alice Huang. The CEO’s statement was followed by more reports of romantic involvement with employees and Nvidia announced that it is probing the CEO and any potential compromise of company secrets or national security. Huang resigned as CEO of the chipmaker last week and the company said earlier this week that its board is not eyeing bringing him back. The company is now being led by former CFO Colette Kress, who has taken over as interim CEO while the company looks for someone to replace Huang.

The Justice Department is separately reviewing Nvidia’s $12.9 billion deal to acquire open-source platform Hugging Face as part of a wider antitrust inquiry into the company’s acquisitions and practices. The department is also probing Megaspeed for potential violations of U.S. export controls involving advanced Nvidia AI chips, though the company itself has denied any wrongdoing.

How Did NVDA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVDA stock stayed within the 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'extremely high' levels.

Stocktwits users continue to debate Jensen Huang’s exit and actions.

data.title: Databricks in early talks to raise funds at $225 billion valuation, WSJ reports
data.description:
Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars in a new round that would value the data and artificial intelligence software company at about $225 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

  • Databricks had said in August it raised $5 billion at a $190 billion valuation, highlighting strong investor demand for companies tied to the AI boom

data.title: Suspect in Los Angeles' deadly Palisades fire convicted of arson at retrial
data.description:
By Steve Gorman

The man accused of deliberately setting the blaze that grew into one of the deadliest, most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history was convicted on Friday of federal arson charges in a retrial of the case, local media reported.

Five months after jurors deadlocked in his first trial, a second US District Court jury found Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, guilty of destroying property by means of fire and arson affecting interstate commerce, according to Los Angeles City News Service and television station KABC-TV. Each offense is punishable by up to 20 years in prison.

The case stems from the Palisades fire in January 2025, which killed 12 people and destroyed some 6,800 structures.

A third, lesser related charge of illegally burning timber was dropped by federal prosecutors after his original trial in June ended in a hung jury.

Prosecutors characterized Rinderknecht, a former Uber driver of US and French citizenship, at both trials as a dejected loner who bore deep resentment against society, particularly the wealthy, and channeled his rage into an act of arson.

He was accused of "maliciously" starting a brush fire on January 1, 2025, that was quickly suppressed but then smoldered underground. It re-ignited days later, whipped by fierce winds, into a conflagration that laid waste to the seaside enclave of Pacific Palisades. Property losses were estimated at $150 billion.

Rinderknecht's defense attorney maintained his client was wrongly accused, suggesting the hilltop New Year's Day blaze was triggered by holiday fireworks and the massive Palisades inferno a week later was a separate fire set by someone else.

The opposing narratives of the disaster left jurors in the first trial deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquittal and unable to reach a unanimous verdict on any charges.

Judge Anne Hwang declared a mistrial, and prosecutors moved to retry the defendant under a grand jury indictment that dropped the timber-burning count and modified the two remaining federal arson counts, a strategy that appeared to have paid off for prosecutors at the retrial.

SIMULTANEOUS DISASTERS

The Palisades disaster coincided with another catastrophic wind-driven wildfire that erupted almost simultaneously in Eaton Canyon, about 30 miles to the east, killing 19 people and ravaging the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena. Fire investigators later concluded that sparks from an electrical transmission tower ignited the Eaton fire.

Rinderknecht was the only person criminally charged in connection with either of the two January 7 blazes, which together rank as the deadliest wildfire calamity ever in Los Angeles County, surpassing the 29 lives lost in the Griffith Park fire of 1933.

Defense attorney Steve Haney had argued at trial that prosecutors lacked sufficient physical evidence or records to prove their case.

In court documents and public statements about the case, Haney also suggested that his client was being scapegoated for failures of the Los Angeles Fire Department.

Prosecutors said security camera footage and location data from Rinderknecht's cellphone show he was the only person in the vicinity of the January 1 blaze when it began near a trail in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.

Rinderknecht, a onetime Pacific Palisades resident himself who has remained in custody since he was arrested in Florida in October 2025, declined to testify in his own defense during either trial.

But he professed his innocence in a court declaration filed in March, denying he had willfully started any fire.

He acknowledged witnessing the outbreak of the January 1 fire from the vantage point of a hill he had climbed to watch New Year's fireworks. But Rinderknecht said he immediately called emergency 911 to report the blaze and remained at the scene until firefighters arrived and offered to help them.

Prosecutors have alleged that while placing his 911 call, Rinderknecht asked the AI app ChatGPT on his phone whether someone could be found at fault for lighting a fire "because of your cigarettes," to which ChatGPT replied, "Yes."

data.title: Wonder explores sale of Grubhub, Wall Street Journal reports
data.description:
Wonder, a food delivery startup led by former Walmart executive Marc Lore, is exploring a sale of Grubhub, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Bankers have contacted Walmart , Target , Kroger and other retailers about a potential acquisition, the report added.

Wonder acquired Grubhub in 2024 for $650 million, including $500 million of senior notes and $150 million in cash. The price was a fraction of the $7.3 billion that European meal delivery group Just Eat Takeaway paid for the business in 2020 during the pandemic-driven boom in food delivery.

A potential sale would come amid broader consolidation in the food and grocery delivery industry.

Rival DoorDash agreed in October to acquire Instacart in a $17 billion deal to strengthen its position in the fast-growing U.S. grocery delivery market as competition among app-based delivery platforms intensifies.

Earlier this year, Grubhub sold its college-campus food delivery business to DoorDash for $300 million. DoorDash also invested $125 million in Wonder as part of the transaction.

There are no guarantees a deal will come together, The Wall Street Journal said, citing the people.

Wonder, Walmart, Target and Kroger did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

data.title: Exxon greenlights $4B Angola oilfield development with new discovery, ANPG says
data.description:
Exxon Mobil and its partners in ​Angola's offshore Block 15 have taken a ‌final investment decision on an estimated $4B redevelopment of the Kizomba A and B fields, while also announcing a hydrocarbon discovery ​in an exploration well, Angola's National Oil, ​Gas and Biofuels Agency said Friday.

The discovery ⁠at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 well was the 21st ​in Block 15 and the second this year and was ​made in one of Angola's most prolific deepwater oil-producing areas, according to ANPG.

The well was drilled to a water depth ​of nearly 4,600 ft and encountered 65.4 meters of sandstone ‌containing ⁠hydrocarbons with good petrophysical properties, ANPG said.

"Supported by the extension of the Block 15 production sharing agreement through 2037 and ~$4B in planned new investments, including the development of the Likembe field and activities under the Block 15 life extension project, we are well positioned to continue generating value for Angola, our partners, and our shareholders," Exxon managing director Brian Unietis said.

data.title: Chicago gas, diesel rises on Midwest pipeline, refinery troubles
data.description:
Cash differentials for gasoline and diesel in the Chicago spot market rose on Friday after issues on an Enbridge pipeline delayed deliveries and prompted at least one refinery to declare force majeure, market participants said.

Chicago CBOB gasoline (CBOB-DIFF-MC) gained 2.5 cents, trading 22.5 cents per gallon below the gasoline futures benchmark on the New York Mercantile Exchange , traders said.​

Chicago ultra-low sulfur diesel (ULSD-DIFF-MC) gained 5 cents, trading 45 cents per gallon below the ultra-low sulfur diesel futures contract on the NYMEX .

Elsewhere in the Midwest, Group 3 V-grade gasoline (RUV-DIFF-G3) fell quarter of a cent, trading 24.25 cents lower than the benchmark.

Group 3 diesel (ULSD-DIFF-G3) fell 7 cents, trading 7 cents lower than the benchmark.

US Gulf Coast M4 conventional gasoline (RU-DIFF-USG) was little changed, trading 3.5 cents lower than the gasoline futures benchmark on the NYMEX, market participants said.

A4 CBOB gasoline (CBOB-DIFF-USG) gained 1 cent to trade at 10.5 cents per gallon above futures, traders said., trading 10.5 cents per gallon below futures, traders said.

Gulf Coast 62-grade ULSD (ULSD-DIFF-USG) fell 3 cents, trading 4 cents per gallon below the ultra-low sulfur diesel futures contract.

In New York Harbor, M4 conventional gasoline (RU-DIFF-NYH) gained a quarter of a cent, trading 18.75 cents per gallon below futures, traders said.

Diesel for delivery in New York Harbor (ULSD-DIFF-NYH) gained 4.5 cents, trading 12.75 cents per gallon above futures, traders said.

The RBOB futures contract on NYMEX rose 0.76 cents to settle at $2.5027 a gallon on Friday, while the NYMEX ultra-low sulfur diesel futures fell 2.98 cents to settle at $3.9216 a gallon.

Renewable fuel (D6) credits (RIN-D6-US) for 2026 traded at $1.91 each on Friday, relatively unchanged from the prior session, while biomass-based (D4) credits (RIN-D4-US) traded at $2.05 each, up 2 cents from the prior session, traders said.

data.title: Brixton Metals Announces Closing of Non-Brokered Private Placement for Gross Proceeds of $1 Million
data.description:
Not for distribution to United States Newswire Services or for dissemination in the United States

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brixton Metals Corporation (TSX- V: BBB, OTCQX: BBBXF) (the “Company” or “Brixton”) is pleased to announce that it has closed a non-brokered private placement offering (the “Offering”) of national flow-through shares in the capital of Brixton (the “FT Shares”) at a price of $0.68 per FT Share. In connection with closing the Offering, the Company issued 1,470,000 FT Shares for gross proceeds of $999,600.00.

The gross proceeds from the sale of FT Shares will be used to incur “Canadian exploration expenses” and “flow-through mining expenditures” as defined in the Income Tax Act (Canada). Exploration expenditures are mainly for exploration and drilling at the Company’s Langis Silver-Cobalt Project in Ontario.

All securities issued in connection with the Offering are subject to a hold period of four months and one day expiring on March 21, 2027 pursuant to applicable Canadian securities laws.

No finder’s fees were paid in connection with closing the Offering.

Option Grant

The Company’s Board has granted incentive stock options (each, an “Option”) to directors, officers, employees and consultants entitling the purchase of an aggregate of 1,840,000 common shares in the capital of the Company at a price of $0.465 for a period of 10 years. The Options will vest immediately with the exception of Options granted to investor relations personnel, which will vest in stages over 12 months from the date of grant with one-quarter of the Options granted to investor relations personnel vesting every three-month period following the date of grant in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

About Brixton Metals Corporation

Brixton Metals is a Canadian exploration company focused on advancing its mining projects. Brixton wholly owns five exploration projects: the Langis and Hudson Bay silver Projects in Ontario; the Thorn copper-gold-silver-molybdenum Project in NW British Columbia; the Hog Heaven copper-silver-gold Project in NW Montana, USA, which is optioned to Ivanhoe Electric Inc.; and the Atlin Goldfields Project in northwest BC. Brixton holds an option to acquire a 100% interest in the silver-focused Silvergruvan Project in Sweden. Brixton Metals Corporation shares trade on the TSX-V under the ticker symbol BBB, and on the OTCQX under the ticker symbol BBBXF. For more information about Brixton, please visit our website at www.brixtonmetals.com.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Belgium's Credit Rating, Warns of High Debt Levels
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Fitch Ratings affirmed Belgium's credit rating and outlook while warning that the country's strengths are somewhat offset by its high levels of debt and political environment.

The credit ratings firm assigned Belgium an A+ sovereign debt rating and a stable outlook due to its diversified and wealthy economy, as well as its membership in the eurozone.

Belgium's public debt is rising and is among the highest in the A rating category, Fitch said. Debt is set to be nearly 110% of gross domestic product by the end of this year, compared with the A rating average of 60%.

The nation's deficit is expected to start rising again in 2029 due to income tax reduction and a further rise in debt interest expenses.

Belgium's structural reforms implemented this year and last should contain social spending, Fitch said. However, fiscal pressure from rising costs persist and the reform measures have sparked protests.

Growth in the country was weaker in the first half of this year than expected, causing Fitch to lower its growth forecast for the year to 0.7%. Private consumption has suffered from higher energy prices, while exports are starting to recover after years of underperformance.

data.title: Quantum Cyber Names Caplon CFO
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Quantum Cyber N.V. named David Caplon chief financial officer following the resignation of William Caragol on Friday.

Caplon succeeds William Caragol, who had notified the defense company on Friday that he was resigning. Caragol entered into a consulting agreement with the company and will receive a fee of $15,000 per month.

Caplon, who became CFO effective Friday, has been the company's controller since June 2026. He has also been corporate controller of CapForce, a financial technology company.

As part of his employment, Caplon will receive a base salary of $22,500 per month and will be eligible to receive a target annual cash bonus equal to 100% of his annual base salary.

Ironman International Ltd. is seeking TSXV acceptance to reduce the conversion price on $500K of debentures from $0.10 to $0.05 per share and extend maturity from November 22 to November 30, 2026. The amendment remains subject to acceptance.

data.title: Lockheed Martin Gets $1.53B Modification to U.S. Navy Missile Contract
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Lockheed Martin received a modification to a Navy contract for up to $1.53 billion to produce missiles.

The defense contractor will be producing and deploying systems support for Trident II missiles in various states across the U.S.

Work is expected to be completed Sept. 30, 2031.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Corn basis steady-higher, soy basis steady-lower
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans were steady to lower in the US Midwest on Friday, while corn basis bids were flat to higher, dealers said.

  • Dealers have been trying to incentivize farmers to sell their crops this week, as US futures prices have been under pressure and the completion of the harvest has kept producers busy.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported on Friday that exporters sold 100,000 metric tons of soymeal to Spain for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year.

  • Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies and, in turn, create more domestic demand for the oilseed in the US, analysts said.

  • CBOT January soybeans settled up 13-1/4 cents at $12.20-3/4 per bushel, bolstered by fresh export demand for soymeal and expectations of tightening US soybean inventories.

  • CBOT December corn ended down 4-1/2 cents at $4.34-1/2 per bushel, though the benchmark March contract stayed above a 4-1/2-month low set one day earlier.
